previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of spinal gunshot wound, neurogenic bladder, and chronic indwelling Foley catheter was admitted for worsening left flank pain concerning for recurrent pyelonephritis. She reported subjective fevers and decreased appetite but was afebrile on arrival with stable vital signs. Initial labs showed mild leukocytosis, but repeat testing revealed decreasing white count. Urine cultures from two separate samples showed mixed bacterial flora consistent with contamination, and renal ultrasound demonstrated no hydronephrosis, stones, or signs of infection. Given the lack of objective infection signs and clinical stability, antibiotics were withheld to avoid promoting resistance. Her Foley catheter was changed on admission, and pain improved with supportive care. She was counseled on the risks of cocaine use and the challenges of suprapubic catheter placement given her unstable housing. She remained afebrile and in no distress, was discharged home with adjusted medications, and connected with social work for follow-up support.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old woman with history of spinal cord injury (secondary 
to GSW age ___ with paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, chronic 
indwelling foley catheter and recurrent multiple drug resistant 
urinary tract infections, presenting to the ED with ___ 
bilateral flank pain.

#. Bilateral flank pain:
Ongoing and at this point appears to be unrelated to urinary 
tract infection. Urine culture still pending with no growth at 
time of discharge. (Later grew out E. Coli and Enterococcus). At 
this admission we decided to treat on indication of complicated 
urinary tract infection with Cefpodoxime for 14 total days given 
that her most recent prior urine culture from ___ showed 
cephalosporin sensitivity. Although we treated with antibiotics 
at this admission, she is likely to be chronically colonized 
with bacteria. She had no fever while in hospital. WBC count was 
slightly elevated at presentation; however, this may have been 
related to pain or cocaine use prior to admission. Foley 
catheter was changed prior to discharge. Patient was given one 
day worth of percocet pills as a bridge to see her new primary 
care physician on afternoon of discharge. She was instructed at 
discharge to follow-up on urine culture final results with her 
new primary care physician.

#. Home medications:
Patient was continued on home fluoxetine, trazodone, 
cyclobenzaprine, amitriptyline. She repeatedly asked for Geodon 
and PPI. No record of her ever taking Geodon was found and thus 
this medication was not dispensed to her. She was given a script 
for Prilosec due to complaints of acid reflux.

#. Substance abuse:
At presentation had urine tox positive for cocaine and admitted 
to smoking crack cocaine ___ days prior to presentation. She 
also admitted to alcohol use, thus was monitored for withdrawal 
during hospitalization, though had no symptoms of this.
 
Medications on Admission:
Fluoxetine 50 mg Capsule daily
Trazodone 200 mg PO HS

Amitriptyline 75 mg Tablet QHS
